name: Herman (1979–84)
description: Republic's first scheme: white, a broad light-blue band under the windows edged in navy below, a thinner light-blue band above the windows, both sweeping up and forward in a point behind the cockpit. 'REPUBLIC' in spaced navy capitals in a gap in the upper band. On the white fin, Herman: a navy ring with a flying duck across it, its long neck reaching forward and a wing raised behind. A navy and light-blue band runs up the fin's trailing edge. Worn by its DC-9s, MD-80s, 727s and Convair 580s until the 1984 'Republic' wordmark scheme.

That interim look isn't this scheme and isn't drawn.

notes: Measured 2026-11-23 on N940N (DC-9-32, left side, 1984) and drawn on the MD-82 (Republic flew both in it); the MD-82 photo shows the same layout. Heights converted from projected to girth shares. Republic never had an ICAO code (it closed in 1986), so it's keyed RC1979. For Skyarium's ghost flights. The Convair 580's paint (types.CVLT) is measured on N968N, 1982. The 727-200's (types.B722) on a 727-2S7 in 1986 and N723RW in 1982, the DC-9-10's (types.DC91) carried from the -30's and checked on N3312L, 1985.

CVLT.note: On the Convair 580 (N968N, Atlanta 1982, sourceRefs 2; measured on shapes/CVLT.json with tools/photo_trace.py's fit and along the body by the nose, the flight deck's aft pane, three windows behind the wing and the tail cone): the bands run straight along the body with a navy pinstripe on the upper band's top edge; the nose's point starts 1.4 m back and its diagonal meets the upper band 5.6 m back, ahead of the propeller; the windows' white strip ends forward in a slanted square end 4-5.5 m back. The title, behind the propeller and over the wing's root, is lower than on the DC-9, its letters reaching below the upper band. The nose is white (no dark radome), the nacelles bare metal. The fin's trailing-edge band is a broad light blue to the trailing edge with a thin navy line along its forward edge, and Herman sits low and forward on the tall fin. Heights are good to about 0.05 of the side (the photo looks up from a few degrees below), positions along the body to about 0.2 m. The 1979-80 photos (sourceRefs 3) show the interim North Central look, not this.

B722.note: On the 727-200 (shapes/B722-passenger.json), measured on two side-on photos: N723RW at Salt Lake City in 1982 (right side, sourceRefs 5) and a 727-2S7 in 1986 (left side, sourceRefs 4), positions along the body by the forward door and the 26 windows behind it, heights against the bands' level runs (the 1986 photo looks up a few degrees: its heights taken down by the window line's offset, then the two averaged; they agree to about 0.07 m). The bands run level: navy -0.42 to -0.14 m, light blue to 0.28 m under the windows, the upper light-blue band 0.825 to 1.195 m with a navy pinstripe on it to 1.28 m. The navy line climbs the nose at about 0.28 m in 1 m from the tip and becomes the pinstripe; the light blue under it comes to a point 1.6 m back; the window strip's front is slanted, 4.4-5.4 m back. 'REPUBLIC' in a gap in the upper band, 8.1-12.7 m back, cap height 0.45 m. Under the side engines the lower bands end in a slant 38.7-39.3 m back; the upper band runs on aft into the fin's band, which comes down the S-duct fairing (the fin's paint carried down). On the fin the navy line and the light blue to the trailing edge stand at about 0.74 and 0.78 of the chord, and Herman sits low, half on the S-duct fairing. White nose; side nacelles bare metal. Positions good to about 0.3 m forward and 0.5 m aft (the 1986 photo's perspective), heights to about 0.07 m.
